predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: Fars, the Salghurid atabegate (Shiraz and the province)

rulers.name: Abu Bakr ibn Sa'd (Muzaffar al-Din Qutlugh Khan)

ledger.x: 1148: Sunqur founds the Salghurid atabegate of Fars at Shiraz.

ledger.cp: holder of Isfahan (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1204: the Isfahan occupation ends ('1203-4'); the page does not say how.
ledger.cp: holder of Isfahan (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1230: Abu Bakr takes Kish Island on 12 November, 'which gave him control over dues on Persian Gulf-India trade'.
ledger.cp: Kish (ruler not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1236: the Salghurids seize the islands of Bahrain in August, 'officially part of the Abbasid Caliphate'; the Salghurids page says they 'occupied Bahrain, which they took from the Uyunid dynasty in 1235'.
1253: end of the occupation, at confidence 1: no page opened says when the Salghurids left Bahrain; the Uyunid page's only dated event is its fall 'to the Usfurids of Banu Uqayl in 651 AH (1253 CE)'.
1282: the Salghurid line ends: 'Following their deaths, Fars was ruled directly by the Ilkhanate.'

wars.name: Salghurid capture of Kish
wars.outcome: Abu Bakr captured Kish Island on 12 November 1230.

wars.name: Salghurid occupation of Bahrain
wars.outcome: The Salghurids seized the islands of Bahrain in August 1236 (Abu Bakr page; the Salghurids page says 1235).

wars.name: Mongol subjugation of Fars
wars.outcome: After Hulagu occupied northern Iran and Baghdad, Abu Bakr declared allegiance by sending his son Sa'd II; Saljuq Shah rebelled and was captured and executed in 1264, when Hulagu had Abish Khatun declared atabeg; a revolt of 1265 was suppressed.

certainty.note: Fars as a province; no frontier on the pages opened.
